newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GIGGS RECALLED TO WALES SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GIGGS RECALLED TO WALES SQUAD.

text.p: Wales manager Bobby Gould said on Friday that Ryan Giggs is relishing the chance to give his country a badly-needed World Cup lift after naming him in a 20-man squad to face Turkey in Cardiff on December 14.
Giggs was making his comeback from a calf injury in Manchester United's reserves when Wales suffered a humiliating 7-1 hammering against the Netherlands in Eindhoven three weeks ago.

Giggs also missed the 3-1 home defeat against the Dutch in October through suspension but hopes to be back for the vital group seven clash with the Turks. Wales have won two and lost two of their qualifiers to date.

"I've spoken to him this morning and he's looking forward to playing for Wales again," said Gould, who added that Giggs hoped to shrug off an ankle injury in time to make his United comeback against Leicester at Old Trafford on Saturday.
Gould also welcomes back skipper Barry Horne and in-form Bolton striker Nathan Blake, who also missed the Eindhoven defeat through injury, and Mark Hughes, who was unavailable through suspension.

But West Ham defender Mark Bowen was dropped with Gould explaining: "He has not been made a scapegoat but I was disappointed with his contribution (in Eindhoven). I've had a chat with him and he understands that."
Vinnie Jones was voted in as skipper for the Eindhoven match in Horne's absence but Gould made it clear it was a one-off arrangement as he had made Horne captain for the qualifying campaign.
Gould said the hammering suffered against Guus Hiddink's stylish side had "knocked some of the players sideways" but he is hoping they can lift themselves for the Turkey clash.
"It took a lot out of them mentally and physically," said Gould, "and now it's all about having a positive mental attitude."
Gould has once again overlooked Wales' record goalscorer Ian Rush, who has yet to score a goal in 15 games for Leeds this season.
Goalkeepers: Neville Southall (Everton), Mark Crossley (Nottingham Forest), Danny Coyne (Tranmere)
Defenders: Steve Jenkins (Huddersfield), Andy Melville (Sunderland), Kit Symons (Manchester City), Mark Pembridge (Sheffield Wednesday), Robert Page (Watford)
Midfield: John Robinson (Charlton), Barry Horne (Birmingham), Gary Speed (Everton), Vinnie Jones (Wimbledon), Andy Legg (Birmingham), Jason Bowen (Birmingham)
Forwards: Ryan Giggs (Manchester U), Dean Saunders (Nottingham Forest), Mark Hughes (Chelsea), John Hartson (Arsenal), Nathan Blake (Bolton), Rob Savage (Crewe).
